item.title: 'The Sopranos' actor Vincent Pastore dead at 80
item.description: Vincent Pastore, who played Big Pussy on "The Sopranos," has died at age 80 at his home in The Bronx, his manager Robert Attermann confirmed.
item.content:encoded:
"The Sopranos" star, Vincent Pastore, died at the age of 80.

The actor's manager, Robert Attermann, confirmed his death to Fox News Digital, saying, "Vinny passed away either yesterday or today at home in The Bronx."

"I had the privilege of representing Vinny for more than 30 years, long before 'The Sopranos' made him a household name," Attermann said. "To the world, he will always be remembered as the unforgettable 'Big Pussy,' but to those of us who knew him, he was so much more."

Pastore was known for his role as Salvatore "Big Pussy" Bonpensiero on the hit HBO Max show, and played a major role as a member of Tony Sopranos clique, before betraying him.

'TOP GUN: MAVERICK' ACTOR JAMES HANDY'S FINAL MOMENTS REVEALED IN AUTOPSY REPORT

In addition to his role on "The Sopranos," Pastore also appeared in "Goodfellas," "A Bronx Tale," "Carlito's Way," "Gotti," ""Once Upon a Time in Brooklyn," "Mickey Blue Eyes" and others.

He also appeared in a number of television projects, including "Blue Bloods," "Law & Order," "General Hospital," "Bull," "Pair of Kings," "Hawaii Five-0" and most recently lent his voice on an episode of "Yellowjackets."

"He loved being an actor," Attermann said. "He was passionate about his craft and was always encouraging, respectful, and generous with young actors, taking the time to offer guidance and support whenever he could."

Pastore also competed on a number of reality competition shows, including "Dancing with the Stars," "Celebrity Fit Club" and "Celebrity Apprentice."

Attermann referred to Pastore as "one of the kindest, most generous people I have ever known," adding, "He treated everyone with warmth and respect, never turning down a fan who wanted a photograph or an autograph."

"He genuinely appreciated the people who supported him and always made them feel valued," he said. "For me, losing Vinny is deeply personal. Over more than three decades, I had the honor of watching not only his remarkable career but also the incredible person he was. I will miss his friendship, his loyalty, his humor, and his generosity."

He continued: "My deepest condolences go out to his family, friends, colleagues, and the countless fans whose lives he touched. He leaves behind a legacy that extends far beyond his memorable performances. He will be greatly missed and never forgotten. May his memory be a blessing."

Pastore's former co-stars, including Kathrine Narducci and Lorraine Bracco took to Instagram to share their own tributes to the fallen star.

Bracco reposted a photo of the actor on her Instagram story, writing, "Such a funny & charming man…just a beautiful soul. Absolutely heartbreaking."

Narducci shared a photo of the two of them on her feed, captioning the post, "This one is crushing , With the most heavy heavy heart I lost my Dearest Big brother friend Vincent Pastore . 35 years of friendship . This is a tremendous loss."

Pastore is survived by his daughter Renee.

item.title: Sophie Cunningham shares touching moment with young Fever fan after game against Portland
item.description: Sophie Cunningham silenced Portland Fire fans waving transgender flags with a three-pointer, then shared a heartwarming moment with a young girl postgame.
item.content:encoded:
There was a lot of intensity in the building when the Indiana Fever paid a visit to the Portland Fire on Friday night.

Most of that intensity came from leftist fans who were upset that Fever star Sophie Cunningham voiced her support for keeping biological men out of women's sports. A stance you'd think is universal among female athletes and fans of women's athletics in general... but here we are.

However, Cunningham didn't let that get to her; in fact, she did the exact opposite, and it was summed up nicely in a heartwarming moment with a young fan after the game.

FEVER SHUT DOWN SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM QUESTIONS, ABRUPTLY END PRESS CONFERENCE

Cunningham was welcomed onto the court in Portland with boos and fans waving transgender flags, and she quickly shut them up by burying a three-pointer and sending a quick message of her own.

Cunningham finished the night with 13 points and 3 assists, and the Fever went on to win 112-98 thanks in large part to a triple-double from Caitlin Clark.

But after the game, Cunningham showed that she practices what she preaches.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

In the ESPN profile that sparked the events of the past week, Cunningham talked about wanting to "protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

So, after what had to be one of the more intense games of her WNBA career, Cunningham had an incredible moment with a young fan in which she gave her one of her game-used shoes.

Hang on to that shoe, young lady; those things are tough to find these days.

What a moment, and one that the young girl will never forget. You can also see that Cunningham's willingness to support women and girls is being felt, and in this case very much appreciated.

As Riley Gaines recently pointed out, the WNBA is at a crossroads where it must decide whether its priority is growing the next generation of girls who will one day join its ranks or political activism.

I think this is a pretty good example of why the former is the right choice.

And yet, if you ask some of the people protesting in Portland — which is like the city's official pastime at this point — or the co-owner of the Seattle Storm, Cunningham is the villain in all of this.

Yeah... okay.

item.title: How often are married people having sex? What to know about the intimacy standard in America
item.description: Research reveals once a week may be the sweet spot for marital satisfaction, with no added happiness boost from more frequent sexual intimacy.
item.content:encoded:
New survey data offers a snapshot of how often married Americans are having sex, while researchers say the findings challenge common assumptions about relationship health.

National demographic studies suggest that lower sexual frequency is often a normal part of aging and long-term relationships, and that there may be a "sweet spot" associated with marital satisfaction.

Data from the General Social Survey, conducted by NORC at the University of Chicago, found that married Americans report a wide range of sexual frequency.

WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATIONS COULD IMPACT SEXUAL HEALTH IN UNEXPECTED WAYS

The survey asked how often couples have had sex during the last 12 months. Among the 1,893 married respondents surveyed in 2024, the responses were as follows.

The average American adult has sex 53 times a year — or a little more than once per week, according to research by the telehealth platform Hims.

While marriage is often associated with less frequent sex, research has found the difference to be relatively small. A 2014 study found that married people had sex about 55 times a year, compared with 59 times a year among their unmarried peers.

"Experts aren’t sure precisely why this difference exists or why what used to be an advantage has become a disadvantage, but some believe it may be related to the increasing age at which most people get married," Hims wrote in a medically reviewed article.

"There’s no ‘perfect statistic’ or ideal amount of sex. In other words: You like what you like, and that’s perfectly OK."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Clinical data suggests that aiming for a daily or high-volume sexual quota does not actually improve relationship quality.

A study published in Social Psychological and Personality Science in 2015 evaluated more than 30,000 individuals over four decades and discovered a drop-off in additional benefits.

While overall happiness increased as physical intimacy moved from monthly to weekly, couples who had sex two, three or four times a week experienced no additional statistical boost in marital satisfaction compared to those hitting the weekly threshold.

Experts emphasize that sexual desire naturally fluctuates as couples navigate career demands, parenthood and biological aging.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Despite some research suggesting a slowdown with age, intimacy remains an important factor in healthy aging, linked to improved physical and emotional well-being.

AARP survey data indicates that physical connection remains routine for many older Americans, with roughly 17% of adults aged 70 and older engaging in sexual activity on a weekly basis.

When a couple experiences an intimacy dry spell, medical professionals recommend evaluating physiological factors rather than jumping to conclusions about incompatibility.

Educational resources from the International Society for Sexual Medicine note that the following physical conditions can influence libido.

Rather than trying to force a weekly goal, healthcare providers encourage couples dealing with mismatched sexual desire to discuss the issue openly and consult a doctor to evaluate baseline hormone levels, medication profiles and overall metabolic health.

item.title: Explosion at restaurant in central Moscow leaves three dead, more than a dozen injured
item.description: A homemade explosive device killed three people at a Moscow restaurant, and injured many more on Saturday night, Russian officials said.
item.content:encoded:
Three people were killed on Saturday at a restaurant in central Moscow following a massive explosion.

The explosion was caused by a homemade explosive device, Russia's National Anti-Terrorism Committee claimed.

The dead included a woman who attempted to bring the explosive device into the restaurant, a security guard and a patron, Russian state news agency RIA Novosti reported.

At least 21 more people were injured in the explosion, which happened around 8 p.m. on a ground floor terrace restaurant​ at Kudrinksaya Square, which includes seven skyscrapers built during the Stalin regime.

A Russian outlet said the explosion happened at the Balzi Rossi ⁠Italian ​restaurant. Its website said it was closed Saturday for a private event.

Heavily armed law enforcement was seen at the scene.

item.title: ICE arrests illegal immigrant accused of rape, multiple sex crimes after release from Maryland jail
item.description: ICE agents arrested a Guatemalan illegal immigrant accused of rape and indecent assault in Arlington, Massachusetts, after his release from state custody.
item.content:encoded:
A Guatemalan illegal immigrant charged with rape and multiple other sex crimes in Massachusetts was arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers after his release from state custody, federal officials said Tuesday.

ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations officers in Boston arrested Rocael Ordonez-Cruz, 23, on July 21 at the Middlesex County House of Correction in Billerica, Massachusetts, according to the agency.

ICE said Ordonez-Cruz entered the United States illegally at an unknown location and time without being inspected, admitted or paroled by a U.S. immigration official.

ICE LODGES DETAINER FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED OF TRYING TO DISARM VIRGINIA POLICE OFFICER

The Arlington, Massachusetts, Police Department arrested Ordonez-Cruz on June 25, according to ICE.

Local authorities charged Ordonez-Cruz with rape and assault to rape.

He also faces charges of indecent assault and battery on a person aged 14 or older, as well as indecent exposure, according to the agency.

EXCLUSIVE: DHS BLASTS SANCTUARY LEADERS AFTER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED OF BAT ATTACK FREED FROM JAIL

"Rocael Ordonez-Cruz has not only displayed a blatant disregard for our laws by illegally entering this United States and later allegedly sexually assaulting our residents, he has also proven to be a threat to our neighborhoods," acting Enforcement and Removal Operations Boston Field Office Director David Wesling said.

"The arrest of this alleged sex offender from the streets of Massachusetts shows our officers' dedication to the safety and security of our New England communities. We will not stop finding and arresting dangerous criminal alien offenders," he added.

After his release from state custody, ICE officers arrested Ordonez-Cruz and served him with a notice to appear before a Justice Department immigration judge.

The notice to appear initiates removal proceedings before an immigration judge.

Ordonez-Cruz will remain in ICE custody pending the outcome of those proceedings, according to the agency.

Fox News Digital reached out to ICE for clarification regarding the circumstances of Ordonez-Cruz's arrest but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Lettuce farmers plow crops back into soil as cyclosporiasis fears tank demand for fresh greens
item.description: A California farmer was forced to destroy 300,000 pounds of romaine hearts as the cyclosporiasis outbreak crushes lettuce demand across America's Salad Bowl.
item.content:encoded:
The nationwide cyclosporiasis outbreak has forced some American farmers to throw out their entire lettuce crops, according to a report.

One such farmer in California’s Salinas Valley told the Wall Steet Journal this week that he had to chop up 300,000 pounds of romaine hearts and plow it back into the soil.

This came with no evidence that his crops were infected with the parasite causing explosive diarrhea that has sickened thousands of people in nearly every state.

WHITE HOUSE ADDRESSES GROWING PARASITE OUTBREAK AFTER MORE THAN 400 AMERICANS SICKENED

Cox’s Coastline Family Farms supplies major grocery stores and top restaurants around the country, but the outbreak has lowered the demand for his greens by as much as 30%, he said.

"It is incredibly demoralizing," Cox told the Journal. "I would’ve been better off taking a vacation in the South of France than planting the crop."

The region is known as "America’s Salad Bowl" and supplies the country with nearly half of its lettuce.

CYCLOSPORA OUTBREAK: IS IT STILL SAFE TO EAT AT RESTAURANTS? HERE'S WHAT TO KNOW

Still, he’s optimistic about the next harvest.

"You can’t afford to be downcast very long. You better pick yourself up, dust yourself off and keep pushing forward," he explained.

Although the outbreak has been linked to iceberg lettuce from central Mexico recalled by California-based Taylor Farms — the country’s largest lettuce supplier --- it’s affected the entire lettuce industry as Americans worry.

CRUISE SHIP HIT WITH THIRD STOMACH ILLNESS OUTBREAK IN TWO MONTHS, REVIEW UNDERWAY

"Consumers aren’t sure what’s right anymore so, out of an abundance of caution, they’re just passing on everything," Joelle Mosso, a food scientist at family farm trade group Western Growers, told the Journal.

Viraj Puri, who founded Gotham Greens in Brooklyn told the Journal that, despite lagging sales, his company opted against less seeding.

"The public health benefits of a diet grounded in fruits and vegetables are indisputable," he said. "I really hope consumers can get back to trusting the fruits and vegetables they buy in stores, because they generally are safe."

Nationally, sales of fresh lettuce fell by nearly 9% in the month between mid-June and July as compared to the same time last year, the outlet reported, citing data from NielsenIQ.

That’s equivalent to 7.6 million pounds of lettuce.

Sales were also down on other vegetables like cauliflower, carrots, spinach and Brussels sprouts.

Even salad dressing has taken a hit.

After one outbreak of cyclosporiasis was linked to lettuce served at Taco Bell, its sales went down by 25% that week.

While some are heading to local farmers markets, hoping their lettuce is more safe, most people appear to be taking a vegetable pause.

item.title: ‘Home Improvement’ star Jonathan Taylor Thomas makes rare appearance in reunion photo with co-stars
item.description: The rare "Home Improvement" cast reunion photo captures Jonathan Taylor Thomas in one of his few public appearances since stepping away from fame.
item.content:encoded:
Jonathan Taylor Thomas is back in the spotlight — at least momentarily.

The former child star appeared in a rare reunion photo with his "Home Improvement" co-stars Patricia Richardson and Taran Noah Smith.

Patricia Richardson sparked a wave of nostalgia when she shared a rare reunion photo with her former "Home Improvement" sons Jonathan Taylor Thomas and Taran Noah Smith, more than 25 years after the beloved sitcom ended.

‘HOME IMPROVEMENT’ STARS TIM ALLEN, RICHARD KARN REUNITE FOR NEW COMPETITION SERIES ‘ASSEMBLY REQUIRED’


"My other boys," Richardson captioned the snapshot with a heart emoji.

For eight seasons of the hit comedy series, Richardson played Jill Taylor, the wife of Tim Allen's character, Tim "The Toolman" Taylor. Thomas and Smith became household names, playing sons Randy and Mark Taylor, respectively, while Zachery Ty Bryan portrayed oldest son Brad.

The reunion offered fans a rare glimpse of Thomas, who largely stepped away from Hollywood after becoming one of the biggest child stars of the 1990s.

Thomas rose to fame as Randy Taylor on "Home Improvement" and became a major teen heartthrob, appearing in films including "Tom and Huck" and "Man of the House." He also voiced young Simba in Disney’s 1994 blockbuster "The Lion King."

But at the height of his fame, Thomas made a surprising decision to walk away.

"I'd been going nonstop since I was 8 years old," Thomas told People in 2013. "I wanted to go to school, to travel and have a bit of a break."

Thomas left "Home Improvement" during its eighth and final season, with his character moving to Costa Rica.

Although he largely stayed out of the spotlight, Thomas briefly returned to acting, reuniting with TV dad Tim Allen on "Last Man Standing" from 2013 to 2015. He appeared in four episodes and directed three.

Smith also left acting behind after "Home Improvement" wrapped in 1999.

PATRICIA RICHARDSON SAYS CHEMISTRY WITH TIM ALLEN MADE HER TAKE THE PART ON ‘HOME IMPROVEMENT’

The former child star went on to explore a series of unexpected careers, including creating a vegan food company, working as an installation artist and helping develop energy-efficient water purification systems used overseas.

His post-Hollywood years also came with controversy. Smith married Heidi Van Pelt at 17, when she was 16 years older, and the couple divorced in 2007. He later became involved in a legal battle with his parents over control of his reported $1.5 million trust fund before eventually reconciling with his mother.

The "Home Improvement" reunion also comes as fans continue celebrating the show's legacy — and the chemistry between Allen and Richardson that helped make it a 1990s television staple.

Richardson previously told Fox News Digital that Allen deserved more recognition for his acting abilities during the show's run.

"People don't give Tim enough credit for the acting that he was doing," Richardson said.

"He had never acted before. He was getting acting lessons on the side."

Meanwhile, Zachery Ty Bryan, who played oldest son Brad Taylor, went on to appear in projects including "Buffy the Vampire Slayer," "Veronica Mars" and "The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift."

Bryan has faced multiple legal issues in recent years. In early 2026, he was sentenced to 16 months behind bars after pleading guilty in connection with a 2024 DUI arrest.

Decades after "Home Improvement" ended, the reunion photo brought fans back to the Taylor household — and reminded them of a cast whose lives took very different paths after leaving one of the biggest sitcoms of the '90s.

item.title: Hundreds block Florida interstate in alleged street takeover before 140 mph police chase
item.description: Traffic cameras captured hundreds of vehicles blocking I-75 in Hillsborough County during an illegal street takeover before a BMW fled at 140 mph.
item.content:encoded:
Four people were arrested after authorities said hundreds of vehicles blocked all northbound lanes of Interstate 75 during an apparent street takeover in Hillsborough County, Florida early Saturday, prompting a high-speed chase that reached 140 mph.

The incident began around 1:30 a.m. near mile marker 266 in Thonotosassa, where Florida Highway Patrol traffic cameras captured a large gathering of vehicles stopping traffic while some drivers performed burnouts in the middle of the interstate, according to an arrest report.

As troopers responded to the scene, video showed vehicles rapidly dispersing as drivers and spectators rushed back to their cars, the report said. While most of those involved were allowed to leave without facing charges, one green BMW allegedly sped away from the scene, leading a trooper to initiate a pursuit.

FLORIDA MAN IN BUNNY HELMET ALLEGEDLY LED POLICE ON 120 MPH CHASE BEFORE SURRENDERING TO TROOPERS

According to FHP, the BMW accelerated to approximately 140 mph — about twice the posted speed limit — before exiting the interstate and eventually stopping in a parking lot.

The driver, identified as 25-year-old Yulian Lugo, was arrested and charged with aggravated fleeing to elude and participating in a street takeover, both felony offenses, authorities said.

Three passengers — a 24-year-old and two 18-year-olds — were also taken into custody and each charged with misdemeanor highway racing, according to FHP.

All four were booked into the Hillsborough County Jail.

VIRAL TEEN TAKEOVERS UNLEASH CHAOS NATIONWIDE AS MALLS, BEACHES AND RESTAURANTS BECOME BATTLEGROUNDS

Street takeovers, in which participants use public roads to perform stunts such as burnouts and other reckless driving maneuvers while crowds gather to watch, have become an enforcement focus for law enforcement agencies in Florida and across the country because of the safety risks they pose to motorists, participants and spectators.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Florida Highway Patrol for additional information, including whether investigators expect to make additional arrests or release dashcam or traffic camera video of the incident.

item.title: Father of 10-year-old boy breaks silence after viral beach rescue: 'No way I could ever repay him'
item.description: Viral video shows 16-year-old lifeguard Ryder Williams diving beneath heavy surf to rescue an unconscious 10-year-old boy at Seabright State Beach.
item.content:encoded:
Sumit Rai said he received a phone call no parent wants to receive after his 10-year-old son was swept into the ocean at California's Seabright State Beach.

"My son [called and] told me, 'Dad, I drowned. I went unconscious.' I'm listening to him, and he thinks he is going to die," Rai shared on Fox News Live.

Nathaniel was standing on the wet sand near the shoreline when a wave knocked him down and pulled him roughly 15 yards into deep water.

TRUMP SAYS HEROIC TEEN LIFEGUARD WHO SAVED BOY FROM TOWERING WAVES DESERVES WHITE HOUSE HONOR

Seabright State Beach was under a high surf advisory at the time. According to California State Parks, swell conditions generated 4- to 6-foot waves, with sets occasionally reaching 10 feet.

Ryder Williams, a 16-year-old lifeguard stationed at Tower 2, spotted Nathaniel losing his footing. In a statement to California State Parks, Williams said he saw the child about 20 yards from the tower.

The 16-year-old radioed in the situation, left his devices and sunglasses at the base of the tower, and ran toward the shore with fins strapped to his wrists and a buoy. He then dove into the water and swam to reach the boy.

Viral video of the rescue showed Williams holding Nathaniel in the rough surf.

CALIFORNIA LIFEGUARD SPEAKS OUT ON HEARTSTOPPING OCEAN RESCUE: 'I LOVE WHAT I DO'

"After the first wave, I was unable to pull him out because he was limp and the waves were pushing so hard," Williams said.

About three more waves broke over the two before fellow lifeguard Aaron Bohnen entered the water to assist.

Rai noted that carrying the limp child required Williams to move roughly 100 pounds through the crashing waves.

"Doing that is remarkable," Rai said. "There is no way I could ever repay him."

OFF-DUTY ICE OFFICER RELIES ON 'SIXTH SENSE' TO SAVE DROWNING CHILD BEFORE DELIVERING MESSAGE TO CRITICS

Williams and Bohnen brought Nathaniel to shore and evaluated him for injuries. Rai, who was not on vacation with his children, said he had not yet seen his son following the rescue.

"The first thing I’ll do is give him a big hug," he said. "... I’m so relieved and grateful for Ryder and his courage and heroism and going into that tumultuous condition to save my son. Without him, my son wouldn’t be alive."

After the video of the rescue garnered national attention, President Donald Trump said Williams deserved a trip to the White House and a national honor.

Asked about the remarks by Fox News Live host Aishah Hasnie, Rai supported recognition for the young lifeguard.

"He absolutely should. I’m for any award or recognition," he said. "I’m his biggest fan, and I am so grateful for what he did. My children are precious to me and nothing means more to me."

Reflecting on the value of local lifeguards in the community, Williams said he feels fortunate.

"I’m grateful to have had the opportunity to return the child to his family safely," Williams said. "This is my job and I love what I do. I’m thankful to my fellow lifeguards who perform rescues just like this every day."

California State Parks’ Santa Cruz District lifeguards performed 34 rescues over the weekend and made more than 5,000 preventative contacts along the coastline.

item.title: 49ers star wide receiver Ricky Pearsall out for the season, to undergo surgery on knee in crushing blow
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers were dealt a massive blow on Saturday, as John Lynch announced that star wide receiver Ricky Pearsall will miss the upcoming season.
item.content:encoded:
Training camp may be early, but the San Francisco 49ers have just taken a massive hit.

Wide receiver Ricky Pearsall will have season-ending surgery on his injured right knee, general manager John Lynch announced Saturday. The surgery will repair his posterior cruciate ligament (PCL).

Pearsall was shut down after two practices in training camp because of swelling in the knee. The 2024 first-round pick has flashed throughout his first two years in the NFL but has struggled to stay on the field.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

As a rookie, he missed most of training camp with a shoulder injury and then was shot in a robbery attempt before the season began. He played in 11 games in 2024, catching 31 passes for 400 yards and three touchdowns.

It seemed like Pearsall was primed to make the jump as the team’s No. 1 receiver in 2025 after catching 20 passes for 327 yards in his first four games, but then he suffered a knee injury. That injury knocked him out for the next six games.

When he returned, he wasn’t as effective as he was toward the beginning of the season, catching five passes for 20 yards over three games. It looked like he was on his way to becoming a key contributor again when he had six catches for 96 yards against the Tennessee Titans before reaggravating the knee injury.

He missed two of the final three regular-season games and the playoff opener before being a nonfactor in a divisional-round loss to the Seattle Seahawks.

Pearsall has 67 catches for 928 yards and three TDs in 20 games over two seasons. Pearsall's lack of playing time makes it unlikely the team would pick up his fifth-year option for 2028 next spring.

To replace Pearsall, the team signed former All-Pro Deebo Samuel on a one-year deal that is worth up to $7 million.

With Samuel, who spent the first six seasons of his career with the 49ers, back in the fold, along with the addition of Mike Evans in free agency and second-round pick De'Zhaun Stribling, the 49ers' receiving corps will look much different.

Samuel was traded to Washington in 2025 for a fifth-round draft pick and had 72 catches for 727 yards and five TDs for the Commanders last season. He became a free agent in March and now will join the Niners to provide reinforcement with Pearsall out.

Samuel has 406 catches for 5,519 yards and 27 touchdowns in his career and has been one of the most dynamic players after the catch in the NFL. His average of 8.7 yards after the catch on receptions ranks first among all receivers with at least 100 catches since 2019. He also has rushed for 1,218 yards and 21 touchdowns in 97 games.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: AOC says MAHA advocates' fight 'isn't partisan' as she blasts healthcare system for fueling 'a ton of anxiety'
item.description: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez says she works with MAHA advocates, pointing to extraordinary corruption in the agricultural and corporate systems.
item.content:encoded:
Far-left Democrat Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., came to the surprising defense of Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) activists, pointing to a "ton of anxiety" within minority and low-income groups around the healthcare system.

During an appearance on "The Majority Report with Sam Seder" podcast, Ocasio-Cortez appeared to side with some of the key topics within the growing health movement and sympathized with Americans who may be wary of the country’s healthcare system.

"I actually meet with MAHA activists. I work with MAHA advocates, because a lot of them really don't believe that their fight is partisan — and it's not in many ways," Ocasio-Cortez said.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS EMBRACE HEALTH AGENDA WHILE RATING RFK JR NEGATIVELY

The movement and its accompanying phrase was previously coined by Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., with the platform taking shape over Americans’ discontent with the country’s healthcare policies.

During Thursday’s episode, Ocasio-Cortez echoed the same discontent to Seder, pointing to the corporatization of certain government organizations.

"We do have extraordinary corruption in our agricultural system, in our big corporate system as well, you know," Ocasio-Cortez said. "This is an area where both parties — and our entire political system — has been compromised."

NEWT GINGRICH: WANT TO REFORM MEDICAID? ACCOUNTABILITY IS THE WAY FORWARD

She went on to recall her previous work in the House of Representatives on PFAS contamination — which are referred to as "forever chemicals."

"One of the first things I did was, when I first got to the House, be part of these congressional investigations on PFAS [Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances] dumping," Ocasio-Cortez said.

"And this goes back decades, where you have a big company that is doing manufacturing of some kind and they just dump whatever cancerous byproduct that they have and poison communities around them," she continued. "And then they just pay off our political class to ignore it and to let it continue to happen, or to shield them legally, like with glyphosate, from everyday people trying to get that back."

WHITE HOUSE ADDRESSES GROWING PARASITE OUTBREAK AFTER MORE THAN 400 AMERICANS SICKENED

Fox News Digital previously covered a 2025 study released by Sweden’s Uppsala University and featured in the "Environment International" journal that revealed two common environmental contaminants, PFAS and PCBs, could increase the risk of multiple sclerosis (MS).

Ocasio-Cortez, who is often viewed as the face of the Democratic Party's socialist movement, also pointed to the rising cost and distrust of healthcare as another contributing factor to the MAHA movement's growing popularity.

"It's because there's a ton of anxiety around our healthcare system," Ocasio-Cortez said.

She went on to offer an anecdote about her own upbringing in a religious household and how her family’s views may mirror those of everyday Americans.

"I grew up in a household that was very much shaped by these dynamics," Ocasio-Cortez said. "My dad's side of the family is Catholic, and I was raised Catholic. But my mom's side of the family is evangelical."

"And I see how all of these issues that have been, at their surface level, expressed as right-wing are actually very much just the anxieties that we have as working people [about] not being able to afford healthcare," she added.

The Democratic congresswoman cited the cost of healthcare as a contributing factor adding to Americans’ anxiety and wariness of the system.

"So it's also like, ‘How do I stop being sick?’" Ocasio-Cortez said. "‘How do I prevent being sick by limiting my exposure to things that I think are toxic?’"

"And then also when I do get sick, and I can't afford medicine, what are the holistic and low-cost alternatives that I can turn to, because I know that I can't afford to see a doctor?" she continued. "And that is a place of tremendous vulnerability that people feel that is immensely legitimate."

Ocasio-Cortez concluded her argument by looking at the racial disparities throughout the healthcare system as well, while suggesting a history of mistreatment and distrust within the medical community toward minorities has done nothing but throw fuel on the fire.

"If you add the racial component too — I'm Puerto Rican, the United States sterilized women for decades," Ocasio-Cortez said. "And so you have COVID, you have vaccines and obviously in the Black community, same thing."

"That is a perfect storm of a lack of trust in institutions that is oftentimes very valid and very legitimate," she continued. "And you don't win that by saying, ‘Oh, don't worry.’ We're condescending to it. We do need to fix our healthcare system."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Department of Health and Human Services for comment.

"What she's doing here is bridge-building, not conversion," Jason Mudd, CEO of Axia Public Relations, told Fox News Digital. "She's not trying to win MAHA activists over to her politics. She's finding the one grievance both sides already share: people don't trust the system that's supposed to protect them, and they can't afford to get sick."

"That's not a left issue or a right issue," Mudd continued. "That's every American's issue."

item.title: Looking back on five of the ugliest college football uniforms the 21st century has had to offer
item.description: From Michigan State's neon fever dream to Iowa State's flesh-colored pants, these five college football uniforms are the worst of the past 25 years.
item.content:encoded:
It's often said that beauty is in the eye of the beholder, but that isn't always the case, and no one knows that better than sports fans.

Sometimes, a team will take the field decked out in some of the most objectively hideous uniforms ever created by mankind, making their supporters and rivals alike question whether they even love the sport anymore.

College football in particular has seen its fair share of eyesores even in the past quarter-century, and with the season rapidly approaching, I thought it would be an appropriate time to recount some of the worst offenders.

JOSH ALLEN DELIVERS FULL-THROATED UNSOLICITED DEFENSE OF BUFFALO BILLS' HIDEOUS NEW UNIFORMS

The five uniforms on this list are all worthy contenders for "worst of all time," but this certainly isn't an exhaustive ranking, so if you think I missed one, feel free to fire away in the comments section.

With that out of the way, suck down some anti-nausea pills, put on a pair of shades, and prepare to be dazzled in all the wrong ways.

Michigan State's Neon Fever Dream

Okay, let's get this one out of the way right off the bat.

I'm sure when you read the title of this article, this little number was one of the first jerseys on your mind.

Everything about it is so preposterous and "anti-Spartan:" the neon STATE emblazoned across the chest (that's too big to even fully fit) the slightly lighter shade of highlighter green pants creating a dissonant clash with the jersey, the neon "Sparty" logo, it's all just awful.

When I think of Michigan State, I think of Mark Dantonio, disciplined football, hard-nosed defense, none of which conjure images of what looks like an alternate Seahawks uniform that a 10-year-old fan designed in a contest.

JOE FLACCO WENT OFF ON SHEDEUR SANDERS FOR WEARING A HELMET VISOR LAST SEASON: 'YOU LOOK LIKE AN IDIOT'

It's a bad uniform on its face, but the fact that it doesn't fit Michigan State's vibes at all puts it over the top.

Thank the Good Lord Sparty stopped larping as Oregon.

Now if they could just find a decent coach...

Florida's "Gatorskin" Extravaganza

Ah, yes! Another easy target for trolls, it's the "Gatorskin" uniforms worn by the boys of old Florida (also known as "Swamp Green").

As many of you are probably presently aware, I'm a huge Gator fan, so these hit a little too close to home.

The powers that be at the University of Florida decided to bust these bad boys out for a game in 2017 against Texas A&M, and the backlash was so loud and universal, that they haven't seen the light of day again in almost a decade.

That probably isn't changing anytime soon, and for good reason.

Conceptually, I see the vision. Alligators are a cool and unique mascot, and the idea of a gator hunting its prey in "The Swamp" is a neat one.

But the execution was dead on arrival, with the whole thing falling flat on its face.

The different colored pants are a brutal look, and opting to go with scales for the tops and not the bottoms was an odd choice.

The orange lettering is garish, and the Gator head logo on one side of the helmet makes this look like an EA Sports "create-a-team" castoff.

I will say it's not my least favorite Gator uniform (see: 2005 vs. Georgia), but it's the most infamous, thus earning its spot on the list.

Georgia's "Silver Bullet" Blunder

The Georgia Bulldogs have some of the cleanest and most iconic uniforms in all of college football, as much as that pains me to say.

So when they trotted these monstrosities out in front of an unsuspecting public at the 2011 Chick-Fil-A Kickoff against Boise State, fans all over the nation rightly winced.

For some reason in the early 2010s, Nike decided to "modernize" a handful of the most recognizable jerseys in college football with their "Pro Combat" series, and this was one of the worst of the bunch.

WISCONSIN FOOTBALL TEAM GETS UNIFORM REVEAL FOR MATCHUP AGAINST NOTRE DAME AT LAMBEAU FIELD

Why is the helmet gunmetal grey? Why is there a giant red stripe running down the middle of said helmet that's about six inches too wide? What's with the black sleeves?

All great questions that no one seems to have answers for, but I keep coming back to the fact that Georgia has great traditional uniforms and an awesome color scheme, so how did they mess this up so badly?

It probably doesn't help the legacy of these kits knowing that Georgia got manhandled by Boise State in what is essentially their backyard of Atlanta.

Luckily for all parties involved, these bad boys have been in the storage shed outside Sanford Stadium presumably since the bus parked on the ride back from this game 15 years ago.

Let's keep it that way.

Maryland's Flag Faux Pas

I'm all for having some pride in your home state, but when your flag is as busy as Maryland's is, plastering it all over every piece of equipment you have feels like you're just trying to torment the viewers.

The Maryland Terrapins rolled these suckers out in the early 2010s and subsequently burned the retinas of college football fans all over the country.

There's just so much going on with these uniforms, it almost seems like an unfair advantage to the team trying to defend Maryland's offense while they wore them.

It feels like the Terps should have come with an epilepsy warning while wearing these, but I digress.

The worst part is Maryland has a very cool and unique mascot of their own in the Terrapin, and they really don't take advantage of that as much as they should.

I'm not saying they need to go the Gators' route and unveil a "Turtleskin" combo, but they've really gone away from featuring Testudo (their mascot) in recent years.

Let's get back to "fearing the turtle," shall we?

The Iowa State "Pooh Bear" Debacle

All of the uniforms on this list are ugly, but these are just downright obscene.

You would think the idea of "flesh-colored football pants" is something that was universally agreed upon as a bad idea a long time ago, but Iowa State committed a cardinal sin of fashion no more than a few years ago.

Hundreds of thousands of people turned on their TVs to see the Cyclones take on TCU on national television back in 2023, only to need a triple take to make sure a bunch of grown men weren't playing football completely bottomless.

They're throwbacks, sure, but no one thought to maybe make the pants a different color?

Take some artistic liberties! For crying out loud, there are kids watching!

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

Somehow, they looked even worse during warmups, as members of the fanbase caught photos from the stands of what looked like a bunch of guys who slept in white tee-shirts and nothing else then rolled out of bed and made their way to the stadium.

I'm not sure how you get something like that so wrong in 2023, but here we are discussing it courtesy of the marketing geniuses in Ames, Iowa.

I'm sure enough people on social media laughed these out of existence, so thankfully we won't be seeing the "Pooh Bear" experiment again anytime soon.

item.title: Toxic, bone-crushing fish from Hell terrorizes vacation waters
item.description: The silver-cheeked toadfish carries deadly tetrodotoxin and has bone-crushing jaws that can sever fingers, prompting Greek authorities to install barriers.
item.content:encoded:
A species of puffer fish with toxic flesh and bone-crushing jaws is expanding its range throughout the Mediterranean, causing local authorities to issue warnings to tourists about the risk of bites.

Some places are even taking precautions to protect swimmers and bathers from the invasive silver-cheeked toadfish, also called harefish.

The fish reportedly entered the Mediterranean through the Suez Canal and has spread as sea temperatures have warmed. It carries tetrodotoxin, a deadly neurotoxin found primarily in its flesh and internal organs, and its powerful beak-like jaws can shred fishing gear and bite through bone.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Experts note, however, that the fish does not routinely attack people. Bites tend to occur when people try to catch, handle or otherwise interact with them.

A 2024 study published in the peer-reviewed journal Toxics documented 198 human-health incidents involving invasive puffer fish across the eastern Mediterranean between 2004 and 2023.

There were 28 records of physical attacks, at least 144 non-lethal poisoning episodes and 27 human fatalities resulting from consumption of the fish, the study found.

"The number of recorded incidents greatly increased after 2019, especially with regard to poisonings, yet whether this is related to greater media attention, or to increased fish abundance is unclear," the researchers wrote in their study.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The Hellenic Red Cross, Greece's national Red Cross society, issued a public advisory in June cautioning that the fish’s flesh "contains a potent neurotoxin (tetrodotoxin), which makes it extremely dangerous to eat," The Times, a U.K.-based newspaper, reported.

"Because the distribution of the toxin varies, no part of the fish is considered safe to eat," the Red Cross warned. "Although the harefish’s bite is not venomous, its extremely powerful, beak-like jaws can cause serious injuries and heavy bleeding."

According to The Associated Press, the fish has "prominent, humanlike teeth," and "its skin and organs contain a powerful neurotoxin that can cause heart failure in humans if consumed."

Tetrodotoxin causes paralysis and respiratory failure. Cardiac effects can occur in the event of severe poisoning.

Greek authorities established floating barriers beneath the Gulf of Euboea between the Greek mainland and the island of Evia to safeguard people in the water, the Guardian reported.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"Our duty and primary concern has to be the safety of our citizens," Antonis Spanos, the vice-mayor of Evia's capital, Chalkida, told the publication. "It’s better to be safe than sorry.

"Two and a half kilometers of this net will be set up in bays around the gulf to allow for a carefree summer," he added. "Last year it was bad with the jellyfish, but, as you say in English, we’ve killed two birds with one stone. Now if there are puffers, we’ll be ready for them too."

Other municipalities along the Gulf of Euboea are also installing or planning to install floating barriers and protective nets to help keep swimmers safe, according to reports.

"Authorities say the fish have not been sighted in bathing areas at Greek island resorts," reported the AP. "But in recent weeks, the fish have wreaked havoc for fishermen off the coast of Crete and several other Greek islands, chomping through nets."

The silver-cheeked toadfish has few natural predators in the Mediterranean, so its population to grow rapidly. The Greek government announced it would pay fishermen 5.33 euros per kilogram, equivalent to about $2.75 per pound, to catch the nuisance fish.

Not all pufferfish are poisonous, but the vast majority contain a lethal neurotoxin called tetrodotoxin in their internal organs and skin. Toxicity levels vary significantly by species, and farm-raised pufferfish that never eat toxin-containing prey in the wild remain non-toxic.

item.title: Henry Winkler dishes on the 'Happy Days' guest star who had a big ego
item.description: Henry Winkler revealed which "Happy Days" guest star rubbed him the wrong way by repeatedly bragging about fan mail on the ensemble-driven set.
item.content:encoded:
Henry Winkler is sharing which former screen partner didn't leave the best impression on him.

While appearing at a recent fan expo in Tennessee, the 80-year-old actor spoke about the comradery on set of "Happy Days," explaining "on our set, there was no stardom," and how one guest star failed to mesh with the rest of the cast.

"We were an ensemble. We worked hard at making it funny every week," he said. "One guy came on as a guest star, and then he was brought back a few times, and he would mention his fan mail, and I said, ‘You don’t want to talk to me about fan mail, I got 50,000 letters a week.’"

He then explained to the actor that "we don't talk about that on the set" and that "we are all here as one."

HENRY WINKLER SAYS AMERICA DOESN'T EMBRACE OLDER GENERATION LIKE OTHER COUNTRIES DO

Despite the warning, Winkler said the actor "kept doing it," later calling the guest star "an a--back." While he didn't name names, he mentioned that the character the actor portrayed was named Eugene.

Winkler played Arthur "Fonzie" Fonzarelli on the hit sitcom throughout all of its 11 seasons, from 1974 to 1984. After getting his big break on the show, he went on to enjoy a successful career in both film and television, earning a Golden Globe nomination for "Heroes," and starring in "The Waterboy," "Holes" and "Click."

After years in the industry, Winkler is still having new experiences on set, as he recently filmed his first nude scene for the first episode of the third season of "Loot."

"Maya Rudolph is one of my favorites. She is [a] brilliant person and a lovely person. So, when she asked me to be on the first episode of the third season of 'Loot,' I didn't even ask to read the script," he explained.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

He then explained that when he went to his first costume fitting, he was shocked to find "a silk robe that went to there," he said while pointing to his upper thigh. "There was nothing else."

"And then we did it in January on the beach. And I want to say the wind came from every direction," he said. "Parts of my body, large and small. … It was so cold. I was in shock. But then I was with Maya and her wonderful cast."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

While he won two Golden Globe Awards for playing Fonzie, Winkler didn't win his first Emmy Award until 2018, when he was rewarded for his work on the hit show "Barry."

He starred on the show as Gene Cousineau, an acting coach who finds himself striking a friendship with a wanted assassin, played by Bill Hader, for four seasons.

"Be yourself, be honest about your ability, prepare so that you are not a flash in the pan," he said backstage after his win, per Variety.

"When I first started here in Hollywood … I thought of myself as a tree or sapling. I planted. I wanted to grow and be strong until I couldn’t do this anymore. And what a great tree it is."

item.title: 'Wonder Woman' star Lynda Carter stuns fans with age-defying Instagram photos of her in a bathtub
item.description: Lynda Carter, 75, stunned fans with Instagram photos from the "Super Troopers 3" set, including a playful bathtub scene that sparked age-defying praise.
item.content:encoded:
"Wonder Woman" star, Lynda Carter, shocked fans with her age-defying appearance on social media.

"@supertroopers Ride Again!!! Follow them and us (returning cast) For a fantastic road romp!!" she captioned the post. "But....wait for it...the last scene! I'm naked in a bathtub???? Oh noooo, @jaychandreskhar you promised not to show that!"

In one of the photos, Carter is all smiles as she lies outside in a bathtub, with bubbles covering her chest and an elegant updo. Behind Carter is a picturesque view of a lake and greenery, and a martini is seen on a table next to her.

'80S ICON KRISTY MCNICHOL MAKES RARE APPEARANCE 25 YEARS AFTER LEAVING HOLLYWOOD

Other photos show the "Supergirl" actress posing with her arms around her co-stars and crew members on the film in a gray robe.

"My God, is she getting younger?!😍" one fan wrote in the comments section. Another added, "Still absolutely gorgeous 😍, while a third fan chimed in adding, "Can't wait! And @reallyndacarter you look amazing!! You don't age!! ❤️🔥🔥"

When speaking to People in March 2024, Carter shared her secret to looking youthful in her 70s, telling the outlet, "People still recognize me all the time as Wonder Woman," adding that since she hasn't "cut" her face, "I probably look just myself, but older."

Carter rose to stardom with her career-defining role playing Wonder Woman in the eponymous show, from 1975 to 1979. Decades after the show went off the air, fans continue to associate Carter with the iconic character, but she says she doesn't mind.

When speaking with E! News in October 2016, Carter explained that speaking about the show has never been an issue for her.

"I love the character. I love her. I think she stands for so much…I've heard so many great stories," Carter said. item.title: Calvin Ridley recalls fast-casual Mexican meal before offseason stomach bug knocked him out
item.description: Calvin Ridley says he lost 15 pounds in 24 hours from a stomach bug he blames on Chipotle, though the chain has no link to Cyclospora cases.
item.content:encoded:
Gastrointestinal issues have been in the news a lot lately (that's not a sentence I thought I'd type when I walked across the stage to receive my college degree), and now Tennessee Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley is talking about a nasty offseason stomach bug he dealt with.

The culprit?

Well, according to Ridley, it was a meal that he had from a certain fast-casual chain known for slinging burritos, burrito bowls, and any other permutation of protein, rice and toppings your heart desires.

STOMACH BUGS SURGING AS DOCTORS SAY CERTAIN TRAVEL ESSENTIALS COULD SAVE YOUR TRIP

On Saturday, a reporter asked him about an offseason bout with a 24-hour bug.

"Oh, yeah, I did," he said. "I've actually had that a couple of times in my life; maybe three or four times. It's not a good thing. It's like a 24-hour thing, but it really puts you down pretty good."

The Titans star revealed that he actually lost around 15 pounds in just 24 hours.

WEIGHT-LOSS JOKE TURNS SERIOUS AS 'CYCLOSPORA SKINNY' TREND FUELS HEALTH WARNINGS

That's brutal. Bugs like that are 24 hours of hell.

If someone said, "Hey, pick between a stomach bug or being fed feet first into a woodchipper," obviously, I'd pick the stomach bug, but I would briefly weigh the options.

Of course, what with all of the Cyclospora and lettuce hysteria, reporters did their job and asked an important follow-up question about whether or not Ridley's dilemma was because he had eaten lettuce.

"Chipotle," he replied.

Now, come on.

First of all, it's important to note that Chipotle has not been linked to any of the Cyclospora incidents sweeping our nation's restrooms and toilet paper aisles (weird that it's still readily available, unlike the early days of COVID, right?).

We've also reached out to the company for comment on Ridley's situation.

We don't know the source of Ridley's ailment, and it's good that he's doing better, but I'm tired of Mexican food being public enemy No. 1 anytime someone gets an upset stomach.

Whenever anyone's stomach feels a bit off-kilter, they go straight to the Mexican food. Sure, maybe it played a role, but it's unfair to just assume.

I mean, it's to the point that in many people's minds, Mexican food is practically as synonymous with gastrointestinal struggles as Tums and Febreze are.

Sure, it's not going to play as nice with the ol' pipes as some other cuisines, but we all know that going in. If you're scared or have plans, maybe eat a few saltines and play it safe.

item.title: Bill Maher breaks with the left to hammer Anthony Fauci after explosive Senate hearing
item.description: Bill Maher accused Anthony Fauci of telling "actual lies" about COVID-19 origins, saying the lab leak theory was silenced over racial politics.
item.content:encoded:
Comedian and talk show host Bill Maher railed against former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases Director Dr. Anthony Fauci just days after he invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination 111 times during a Senate hearing over his handling of the COVID-19 pandemic.

During Friday’s episode of HBO’s "Real Time," Maher called out Fauci for telling "actual lies" about the origins of the virus responsible for over seven million confirmed deaths worldwide following Fauci’s Senate hearing on Wednesday.

"He was caught in actual lies," Maher said, adding, "The big issue to me is the origin of this, which is very important. How did it start?"

TOP 5 MOMENTS FROM FAUCI'S HEARING: PAUL BOOTS LAWYER, MORENO ERUPTS AS CONTEMPT VOTE LOOMS

The comedian pointed to Fauci’s previous assertions that the virus originated through animal-to-human contact at a wet market in Wuhan, China.

"He was telling people up front when it first began [that] it was from the wet markets. It could not — that's a conspiracy theory — if you say it escaped from the lab," Maher said.

"And he knew better," Maher continued. "Because we have him in his diary telling us what he was saying to other scientists, who were saying, ‘No, absolutely.’"

Fox News Digital reached out to Fauci for comment.

SLACK MESSAGES RELEASED BY RAND PAUL APPEAR TO SHOW AUTHORS OF KEY COVID-19 ORIGIN PAPER HELD PRIVATE DOUBTS

Maher went on to point to the controversial theory that the virus was the result of either an accidental or intentional leak from a Chinese laboratory in the same city where the first cases originated.

He also blasted Fauci over the crux of his hearing, in which he was questioned regarding the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases’ funding of "gain-of-function" research in China.

Fox News Digital previously covered Fauci’s vehement denial that the controversial research method — which involves scientists altering the genetics of a virus to better understand and treat it — led to the samples breaking free from the Wuhan Institute of Virology.

WATCH: RAND PAUL SAYS THERE'S ONE THING AMERICANS HAVE NEVER HEARD FROM FAUCI

"I would always have said, don't do it, but it's a viable debate," Maher said, referring to the "gain-of-function" research method. "It's a reasonable debate — should we soup up something that's bad, this bacteria, to study it? Maybe if it got out it would be even worse. I think that's what did happen."

In June 2025, the World Health Organization released a report in which officials determined "the weight of available evidence … suggests zoonotic spillover … either directly from bats or through an intermediate host."

Maher then challenged the controversy surrounding the lab leak theory, which has been supported by President Donald Trump, and suggested the outcry surrounding its merit was largely due to social issues — not scientific evidence.

"We could have had that debate in a rational way," Maher said. "We didn't want to do that. Because why? Because we make everything about race. And this is one of the repercussions in this."

Maher added that the pandemic brought a racial stigma surrounding the lab leak theory, creating an unfounded taboo on the topic.

"You couldn't say it escaped from the lab, because that was the racist point of view somehow — that the entire Asian continent would have been somehow complicit in this because it escaped from the [lab]," Maher said. "It was ridiculous."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"But that is where they went," the comedian continued. "You were racist if you said this escaped from a lab. I think we've morphed from a place where we want to obviously not be prejudiced against anybody, to where people of color can never do any wrong."

Maher’s criticism of Fauci marks a notable break from his fellow left-leaning counterparts in media, who have historically stood behind the doctor.

"Once again, Bill Maher is willing to level with the country in a way the liberal, elitist media never would," Curtis Houck, managing editor of NewsBusters at the Media Research Center, told Fox News Digital. "The press should be capable of calling balls and strikes."

"But when it comes to most things and their dear Saint Fauci, they must protect him at all costs by either explaining away his damaging diary entries or not covering them at all," he continued. "The media have made the decision to be joined at the hip with Fauci, even as his credibility has dropped off a cliff."

item.title: Trump says he 'disagrees 100%' with U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro over Reflecting Pool case
item.description: Trump publicly broke with U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro on Truth Social, calling Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool damage a case of "VANDALISM."
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump publicly broke with his top local prosecutor Saturday, insisting damage to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool was "a pure case of VANDALISM" despite federal officials citing contractor failures as they moved to dismiss a felony case against a former U.S. Olympian.

"I disagree 100% with Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, on the Reflecting Pool," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "I don’t know what she was thinking?"

Trump's remarks came one day after Pirro's office asked a federal judge to dismiss a felony destruction of property charge against former U.S. Olympian David Hearn, who was accused of damaging the landmark after allegedly pulling up a loose section of its protective lining on June 19 despite being told by a National Park Service employee to stop.

"To me, it was a pure case of VANDALISM, that included the grass, which had a big 86 47 emblazoned in giant letters on it, and other elements of the surrounding area," Trump continued, referencing a separate vandalism incident that had occurred about a week earlier.

U.S. Park Police previously discovered the numbers "86 47" etched into the grass near the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. The phrase has become a politically charged slogan directed at Trump. Supporters of the president, including Trump himself, have argued it amounts to a call for his assassination.

WHO IS DAVID HEARN? US OLYMPIAN WHO DENIES VANDALIZING REFLECTING POOL AFTER VIRAL ARREST

Pirro's office dropped the charges against Hearn on Friday after concluding that reports disclosed by the Department of the Interior revealed that there were many flaws with the renovation project, including that the lining appeared to begin peeling days after installation.

"Given all of this newly discovered information, it is difficult to attribute the widespread damage to the Reflecting Pool to vandalism, let alone to establish that fact beyond a reasonable doubt," the motion concluded.

Trump acknowledged there potential issues with the project but rejected the Justice Department's conclusion that construction problems were primarily responsible for the damage.

"There may have been some contractor difficulty, but the major damage was caused by VANDALS!" Trump wrote.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION HAS LOST OR ABANDONED HUNDREDS OF LAWSUITS AGAINST ANTI-ICE PROTESTERS, MIGRANTS: REPORT

Hearn was indicted on July 2 on one count of felony destruction of property after U.S. Park Police alleged he pulled at the pool's protective coating, with authorities initially estimating the damage exceeded $1,000.

According to Pirro's office, the Department of the Interior initially provided only "barebones" reports and did not disclose documents showing the Reflecting Pool's newly installed coating had begun failing almost immediately after construction.

"Had DOI been forthcoming with the information clearly in its possession, the government would not have sought a grand jury indictment," prosecutors wrote in Friday's filing.

"It was not until after the return of the indictment, that the DOI provided additional documents to the USAO-DC indicating that damage to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in June 2026 was the result of flawed installation by the contractor, Atlantic Industrial Coatings ('AIC'), and the rush to complete the project prior to events associated with the America 250 celebration in the weeks surrounding Independence Day 2026," the filing continued.

The case against Hearn was dismissed without prejudice, meaning charges could be brought again in the future.

Court filings show Atlantic Industrial Coatings received a no-bid contract worth more than $14 million to install a new protective lining across the Reflecting Pool's 68,000-square-foot floor.

The project began in early May but was slowed by rain and complications with the pool's expansion joints, adding pressure to complete the work before the July Fourth festivities celebrating America's 250th anniversary.

According to prosecutors, problems surfaced almost immediately.

TRUMP SHARES NEWS OF 'CRYSTAL CLEAR' REFLECTING POOL, CALLS FOR VANDALISM SUSPECT'S ARREST

Just two days after the project was completed on June 9, a National Park Service engineer reported that sections of the new lining were already peeling.

"I stated my concern that this 'overspray' along the perimeter of the pool could lead to a 1'-2' strip that is vulnerable to peeling," the engineer wrote in a June 11 email obtained by the New York Post. "The contractor would not confirm in field if this was or wasn't a risk."

Following the dismissal request, Hearn's legal team accused the government of rushing to prosecute the case.

"The Trump administration's case against Davey Hearn should never have been brought. Its dismissal today does not erase the abuse of government power in arresting and charging a patriotic American who did nothing wrong. The government’s approach was ready, fire, aim. The administration owes Mr. Hearn an apology," attorneys Norm Eisen, Mary Dohrmann and Steve Levin said in a statement to the New York Post.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Pirro's office for comment.

item.title: Heidi Klum shows off figure during yacht trip after revealing her husband told her to 'eat more'
item.description: Heidi Klum and daughter Leni Klum stun in bikinis on a St. Barts yacht, weeks after the supermodel revealed why she refuses GLP-1 weight loss drugs.

The 53-year-old German supermodel was photographed enjoying time with her daughter, Leni, and her daughter's boyfriend, Aris Rachevsky, on a yacht off the coast of St. Barts in the Caribbean.

In the photos, the mother-daughter duo both stun in bikinis. Klum  rocked a cream-colored string bikini, which she paired with a gray baseball cap and sunglasses, and in some photos she held up her dog as an accessory.

Leni also wore a bikini, flaunting her toned body in a strapless blue top and matching bottoms, which she paired with a white hat and sunglasses.

HEIDI KLUM DITCHES BIKINI TOP, COVERS UP WITH POTATO CHIP BAG ON BEACH VACATION

Some of the photos show Leni wearing a snorkeling mask and flippers, while in others, she is taking photos of her mom, which later appeared on Klum's Instagram.

"You Are so beautiful Heidi 😍💗🔥👑" one fan wrote in the comments section. Another added, "The girlz still got it...🔥🔥"

"Tom is lucky to have an amazing woman like Heidi," a third fan wrote.

The mother-daughter vacation came a few weeks after the "America's Got Talent" judge spoke to Us Weekly about how her husband, Tom Kaulitz, went against one of Hollywood's biggest beauty obsessions and told her to "eat more."

She told the outlet that she is "not interested at all" in GLP-1 drugs, admitting she has gained weight over the past few years. She doesn't mind the weight gain, adding, "I think with age, we look better when we're not as skinny."

"My husband was the first one who pointed that out. He said, 'You should eat more; you would look better if you had more meat on your bones.' I was like, 'What?' This is not something you're told in the industry, ever, because you're always supposed to be skinnier than you are."

item.title: Baby boomers hate 10 things about today's grocery stores
item.description: From self-checkout frustrations to digital coupons and understaffing, baby boomers have strong opinions about how modern grocery stores have changed.
item.content:encoded:
Grocery shopping has changed dramatically over the past 50 years, and not everyone is happy about it.

Baby boomers — generally defined as those born between 1946 and 1964 — are particularly frustrated by many of today's grocery-store features, according to The Takeout. Technology-driven shopping is among their biggest complaints, along with several other modern grocery-store changes.

TRADER JOE'S WORKERS SHUT DOWN LONG-RUNNING CHECKOUT LINE RUMOR: 'OVER-THE-TOP FRIENDLINESS'

When asked to choose between self‑checkout and cashier‑assisted checkout — each with equal lines — 62% of respondents to a YouGov survey aged 65-plus said they preferred cashier-assisted checkout, compared to 34% who said they like self-checkout.

Fifty percent of respondents aged 45-64 said they preferred checking out with a cashier, while 44% said they would choose self-checkout. In the 18-29-year-old demographic, meanwhile, 52% said they prefer self-checkout, while 26% said they would prefer cashier-assisted checkout.

The major hangups boomers have with self-checkout is weighting produce, the lack of human interaction and the feeling they’re doing free labor, The Takeout reported.

Cleanliness and organization are what baby boomers prioritize in grocery stores, a 2024 survey published by the Feedback Group found.

Boomers have a strong preference for supermarkets (32%), the survey found, while Walmart (28%) was their second choice for grocery shopping. Gen X shoppers preferred Walmart (28%), followed by supermarkets (25%), while Gen Z opted for Walmart (23%), Aldi (20%), dollar stores (17%) and club stores (15%). Traditional supermarkets ranked last among Gen Z shoppers, with only 11% reporting this as their go-to store.

Grocery stores carefully arrange products to encourage shoppers to spend more time in the store and buy more items.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Frequent product relocations were another common complaint in the social-media responses highlighted by The Takeout.

The share of people aged 65 and older who are tech-users grew in the last decade, a 2022 Pew Research Center poll found. Despite this trend, many baby boomers say digital-only coupons put shoppers without smartphones at a disadvantage.

Trader Joe’s is an outlier, The Takeout noted, since the grocery-store chain doesn’t offer discounts or sales.

Shopping carts offer a "tactical maneuver" for some older adults who rely on them for mobility and stability purposes and as a rest aid, according to The Takeout.

Several baby boomers reacted to a Facebook post asking about their grocery-shopping experience to say they value shopping carts with wheels that swivel easily and are easy to push.

While younger generations are more likely to shop at budget grocery stores and buy off-brand products, a sizable number of baby boomers always go for name brands.

More than one in four (26%) baby boomers "rarely or almost never consider switching from their favorite brand," a Numerator survey on consumer trends found.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

A Reddit forum featured many commenters expressing frustration with the older generation for spending more money for a comparable, generic product, The Takeout reported.

Many Americans grew accustomed to encountering out-of-stock items when the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted the supply chain. But baby boomers aren’t as accepting of the reality as others, according to social-media posts on the subject.

Many retirees live on fixed incomes and rely on sale-priced products to help stretch their grocery budgets, meaning unavailable items can have a greater financial impact on older adults.

Food retailers have faced recruitment and retention challenges in recent years, and it’s a pattern keenly felt by baby boomers.

Social-media comments summarized by The Takeout suggest many boomers associate understaffing with longer checkout lines, slower service and fewer opportunities for personal interaction with employees.

Going hand-in-hand with frustrations over self-checkout and understaffed stores, many baby boomers also dislike the growing absence of dedicated grocery baggers.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Plenty of boomers complain on social media about this modern grocery-store, expressing frustration at doing their own labor, according to The Takeout.

Millennials, those born between 1981 and 1996, comprise the generation most likely to spend money on prepared grocery meals, a U.S. Department of Agriculture survey found. Prepared meals often cost significantly more than cooking from raw ingredients because shoppers pay for the added convenience.

According to research summarized by the Institute of Food Technologists from FMI’s (originally the Food Marketing Institute) U.S. Grocery Shopper Trends report, 29% of shoppers ages 65 and older reported buying prepared foods to save time, compared with 45% of shoppers ages 15 to 24.

item.title: Fans stunned at Travis Kelce's training camp physique after nuptials to Taylor Swift
item.description: Fans poke fun at Travis Kelce's physique after videos of the Kansas City Chiefs star at training camp surface online just weeks after he married Taylor Swift.
item.content:encoded:
Travis Kelce is turning heads at the Kansas City Chiefs training camp, but not with his play.

NFL LEGEND ROB GRONKOWSKI DETAILS TRAVIS KELCE AND TAYLOR SWIFT'S 'MAGNIFICENT' WEDDING
